newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat European car sales rise in September.
newsitem.headline: Fiat European car sales rise in September.

text.p: Fiat Auto sales are showing a marked improvement in Europe despite problems on the Italian market where group sales fell 17.5 percent year-on-year in September, Fiat said in a statement.
Fiat group marques saw sales in Europe rise 41.47 percent in September.

Apart from the state of the continuing depressed car market in Italy, sales were also influenced by the launch of the Marea and Marea station-wagon on September 15 which limited new registrations in the month.
But orders from Italian dealers totalled 16,000 and would significantly influence data from October onwards, Fiat said.
The positive trend in Europe was confirmed by figures for the January-September period with Fiat Auto sales up 23.7 percent in a European market which grew 8.0 percent excluding Italy.
Fiat Auto sales were up 33.5 percent in Germany last month where the market rose by just 1.0 percent. In France, the market jumped by 86 percent but Fiat sales surged 114.7 percent.
In Britain, where the market slipped 2.0 percent, Fiat sales increased by 35 percent.
